newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's Klima unveils fresh-faced cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Austria's Klima unveils fresh-faced cabinet.

text.p: Austrian chancellor-designate Viktor Klima unveiled his new cabinet on Monday, saying it would breathe much-needed fresh life into the country's stale coalition government.

Klima, making his first public appearance since accepting the job of chancellor and Social Democratic Party leader, presented his new-look team after senior Social Democrats gave it their unqualified approval.
He confirmed the appointment of Vienna city finance chief Rudolf Edlinger to the treasury and the demotion of former interior minister Caspar Einem, darling of the left, to transport.
"This is a team for the future," Klima, 49, told a packed news conference. "This team will help me to bring in reforms, open the window and let in fresh air."

As expected, he named state secretary for public works Karl Schloegl interior minister and promoted Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, a member of the board of the OMV oil company, to the new post of state secretary for finance.
As Edlinger's right-hand man, Ruttenstorfer will attempt to guide Austria into a single European currency.

The new appointments are part of a wide-ranging reshuffle triggered by Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's surprise resignation on January 18. Klima has taken the opportunity to oust prominent leftwingers, like Einem and ex-transport minister Rudolf Scholten, in favour of moderates.
President Thomas Klestil is to swear in the new team on Tuesday. There were no changes to posts occupied by the junior coalition partner, the conservative People's Party.
Klima said the Social Democrats were committed to continuing their 10-year partnership with the People's Party in an atmosphere of "fair and open cooperation".
He dismissed speculation that his party would contemplate forming a coalition with the far-right Freedom Party but he did not rule out future cooperation.

"For the Social Democrats and for me a coalition with the Freedom Party of Joerg Haider is out of the question. We have agreed a government programme and I assume neither coalition party intends to flirt with others," he said.
But he added that the Social Democrats remained open to ideas from the opposition. "I am very open to all ideas, even those that go against Social Democrat principles," he said.
The Social Democrat vote slumped to an all-time low in European elections last October, dipping below 30 percent, while far-right support soared to nearly 28 percent.
Klima will be hoping to revive his party's fortunes through strength of personality. A recent poll gave him a 47 percent approval rating.
The incoming chancellor stressed there would be continuity in key foreign policy issues and said he had no plans to join NATO and abandon Austrian neutrality
"The organisation (NATO) is undergoing major changes. It would be very unwise to abandon our position until we know which direction the various organisations in Europe are developing," he said.
NATO membership has been a bone of contention between the coalition partners, with the People's Party indicating it favours joining the alliance.
